units.zh: 河東之兵無詣懿者，懿深患之。
units.en: No Hedong troops joined Yao Yi; he panicked.
units.literal: Not one Hedong soldier went to Yi; Yi deeply worried over it.

units.zh: 臨晉數千戶叛應懿。
units.en: Thousands in Linjin rose for him.
units.literal: Several thousand households of Linjin rebelled to answer Yi.

proposals.before: Thousands in Linjin rose for him.
proposals.after: Several thousand households in Linjin rose in support of Yao Yi.
proposals.reason: 數千戶 counts households, not people.

units.zh: 姚紹濟自薄津，擊臨晉叛戶，大破之，懿等震懼。
units.en: Yao Shao crossed at Bo ford, crushed the Linjin rebels, and terrified Yao Yi.
units.literal: Yao Shao crossed from Bo ford, struck the Linjin rebel households, greatly defeated them; Yi and others were shaken with fear.

proposals.before: Yao Shao crossed at Bo ford, crushed the Linjin rebels, and terrified Yao Yi.
proposals.after: Yao Shao crossed at Bo Ford and routed the rebel households of Linjin. Yao Yi and his followers were shaken with fear.
proposals.reason: 懿等 includes others besides Yi.

units.zh: 鎮人安定郭純、王奴等率眾圍懿。
units.en: Guo Chun and Wang Nu besieged Yao Yi.
units.literal: Garrison men of Anding Guo Chun and Wang Nu and others led hosts to surround Yi.

proposals.before: Guo Chun and Wang Nu besieged Yao Yi.
proposals.after: Guo Chun, Wang Nu and other garrison men from Anding led their followers in surrounding Yao Yi.
proposals.reason: Restore Anding origin, garrison affiliation and leadership of followers in the encirclement.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼
王師漸逼

units.zh: 紹入于蒲阪，執懿囚之，誅孫暢等。
units.en: Yao Shao took Puban, jailed Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang.
units.literal: Shao entered Puban, seized Yi and imprisoned him, executed Sun Chang and others.

proposals.before: Yao Shao took Puban, jailed Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang.
proposals.after: Yao Shao entered Puban, captured and imprisoned Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang and others.
proposals.reason: Shao entered Puban, captured and imprisoned Yi, and executed Chang and others.

units.zh: 泓以內外離叛，王師漸逼，歲旦朝群臣於其前殿，淒然流涕，群臣皆泣。
units.en: On New Year's Day Yao Hong wept before his court as Jin closed in and kin rebelled.
units.literal: Because inner and outer split in rebellion and the royal army pressed gradually, on New Year's dawn Hong met the host of ministers in his front hall, wept dismally; the host of ministers all wept.

proposals.before: On New Year's Day Yao Hong wept before his court as Jin closed in and kin rebelled.
proposals.after: With defections at home and abroad and the Jin army drawing nearer, Yao Hong received his ministers in the front hall on New Year’s morning. He shed tears of grief, and the ministers all wept.
proposals.reason: The defections are internal and external, and all the officials wept with Hong at the front-hall audience.

sourceDate.text: 歲旦

units.zh: 時征北姚恢率安定鎮戶三萬八千，焚燒室宇，以車為方陣，自北雍州趣長安，自稱大都督、建義大將軍，移檄州郡，欲除君側之惡。
units.en: Yao Hui marched on Chang'an with thirty-eight thousand families in chariot fortresses, claiming he would purge evil counselors.
units.literal: At the time General Who Conquers the North Yao Hui led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households, burned houses, formed a chariot square, went from North Yongzhou toward Chang'an, styled himself grand commander-in-chief and great general who establishes righteousness, circulated call to arms to province and commandery, wishing to remove evil beside the ruler.

proposals.before: Yao Hui marched on Chang'an with thirty-eight thousand families in chariot fortresses, claiming he would purge evil counselors.
proposals.after: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, burned the houses and led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households toward Chang’an from North Yongzhou, forming his wagons into a square. He styled himself grand commander-in-chief and Great General Who Establishes Righteousness and sent proclamations to the provinces and commanderies declaring his intent to rid the ruler’s side of evil men.
proposals.reason: Restore the burning of houses, origin in North Yongzhou, square made with wagons, Hui’s self-assumed titles and proclamation to provinces and commanderies.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 揚威姜紀率眾奔之。
units.en: Jiang Ji rode to his banner.
units.literal: General Who Displays Might Jiang Ji led hosts to join him.

proposals.before: Jiang Ji rode to his banner.
proposals.after: Jiang Ji, General Who Displays Might, led his men to join Hui.
proposals.reason: Jiang Ji led troops with him and held the Yangwei generalship.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 建節彭完都聞恢將至，棄陰密，奔還長安。
units.en: Peng Wandu, who bore credentials, heard that Hui was about to arrive, abandoned Yinmi, and fled back to Chang'an.
units.literal: Jianjie Peng Wandu heard Hui would arrive, abandoned Yinmi, fled back to Chang'an.

proposals.before: Peng Wandu, who bore credentials, heard that Hui was about to arrive, abandoned Yinmi, and fled back to Chang'an.
proposals.after: When General Peng Wandu, holder of the title Jianjie, heard that Hui was approaching, he abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: 建節 is Peng Wandu’s military designation, not an assertion that he carried credentials. Compare the same title on Wang Zong in s0055.

proposals.before: Jianjie Peng Wandu heard Hui would arrive, abandoned Yinmi, fled back to Chang'an.
proposals.after: When General Peng Wandu, holder of the title Jianjie, heard that Hui was approaching, he abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: 建節 is Peng Wandu’s military designation, not an assertion that he carried credentials. Compare the same title on Wang Zong in s0055.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 恢至新支，姜紀說恢曰：「國家重將在東，京師空虛，公可輕兵徑襲，事必克矣。」
units.en: Jiang Ji urged Hui, saying, "The state's weighty generals are in the east; the capital is empty—with light troops you could raid straight in; the affair would surely succeed."
units.literal: When Hui reached Xin-zhi, Jiang Ji urged Hui, saying, "The state's weighty generals are in the east; the capital is empty—with light troops you could raid straight in; the affair would surely succeed."

proposals.before: Jiang Ji urged Hui, saying, "The state's weighty generals are in the east; the capital is empty—with light troops you could raid straight in; the affair would surely succeed."
proposals.after: When Hui reached Xinzhi, Jiang Ji urged him, “The state’s leading generals are in the east, leaving the capital undefended. If you strike straight at it with light troops, you are sure to succeed.”
proposals.reason: The exchange takes place when Hui reaches Xinzhi.

units.zh: 恢不從，乃南攻郿城。
units.en: Yao Hui refused and struck south for Mei instead.
units.literal: Hui did not follow, then attacked south toward Mei city.

units.zh: 鎮西姚諶為恢所敗，恢軍勢彌盛，長安大震。
units.en: Yao Chen lost to Yao Hui; panic gripped Chang'an.
units.literal: General Who Guards the West Yao Chen was defeated by Hui; Hui's army momentum grew ever stronger; Chang'an was greatly shaken.

proposals.before: Yao Chen lost to Yao Hui; panic gripped Chang'an.
proposals.after: Yao Hui defeated Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West. Hui’s army gathered still greater strength, and Chang’an was badly shaken.
proposals.reason: Restore Chen’s title and the increase in Hui’s military strength after his victory.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 泓馳使征紹，遣姚裕及輔國胡翼度屯於灃西。
units.en: Yao Hong recalled Yao Shao and sent Yao Yu and Hu Yidu west of the Feng River.
units.literal: Hong dispatched riders summoning Shao, sent Yao Yu and General Who Supports the State Hu Yidu to camp west of the Feng.

proposals.before: Yao Hong recalled Yao Shao and sent Yao Yu and Hu Yidu west of the Feng River.
proposals.after: Hong sent a rider at speed to summon Yao Shao and ordered Yao Yu and Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to camp west of the Feng River.
proposals.reason: Hong rushed a mounted messenger to recall Shao; Yu and Hu Yidu, who holds the Fuguo title, were to camp west of the Feng.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼
王師漸逼

units.zh: 扶風太守姚雋、安夷護軍姚墨蠡、建威姚娥都、揚威彭蠔皆懼而降恢。
units.en: Several frontier generals went over to Yao Hui.
units.literal: Fufeng Grand Administrator Yao Jun, Protector of the Pacified Yi Yao Moli, Jianwei Yao E'du, General Who Displays Might Peng Hao all feared and surrendered to Hui.

proposals.before: Several frontier generals went over to Yao Hui.
proposals.after: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.
proposals.reason: Retain all four individuals and their offices, including An’yi protector and Jianwei as a military title, and their fear as motive for surrender.

proposals.before: Fufeng Grand Administrator Yao Jun, Protector of the Pacified Yi Yao Moli, Jianwei Yao E'du, General Who Displays Might Peng Hao all feared and surrendered to Hui.
proposals.after: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.
proposals.reason: Retain all four individuals and their offices, including An’yi protector and Jianwei as a military title, and their fear as motive for surrender.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼
王師漸逼
王師漸逼
王師漸逼

units.zh: 恢舅苟和時為立節將軍，守忠不貳，泓召而謂之曰：「眾人咸懷去就，卿何能自安邪？」
units.en: Yao Hong summoned Gou He and asked, "Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay—how can you alone remain at ease?"
units.literal: Hui's maternal uncle Gou He then served as Jianjie general, kept loyalty without wavering; Hong summoned him and said, "The multitude all harbor leaving or staying—how can you alone be at ease?"

proposals.before: Yao Hong summoned Gou He and asked, "Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay—how can you alone remain at ease?"
proposals.after: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”
proposals.reason: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He holds the Lijie (立節) generalship, not Jianjie (建節). He remains undivided in his loyalty.

proposals.before: Hui's maternal uncle Gou He then served as Jianjie general, kept loyalty without wavering; Hong summoned him and said, "The multitude all harbor leaving or staying—how can you alone be at ease?"
proposals.after: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”
proposals.reason: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He holds the Lijie (立節) generalship, not Jianjie (建節). He remains undivided in his loyalty.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼
王師漸逼

units.zh: 和曰：「若天縱妖賊，得肆其逆節者，舅甥之理，不待賓士而加親。
units.en: Gou He said: "If treason wins, uncle and nephew share the stain.
units.literal: He said, "If Heaven lets the demon bandit prevail and he gets to carry out his treason, the principle of uncle and nephew needs no guest-retainer to grow closer.

proposals.before: Gou He said: "If treason wins, uncle and nephew share the stain.
proposals.after: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.
proposals.reason: A Jinshu witness reads 奔馳 for the packet’s 賓士, confirmed independently by the parallel in Shiliuguo chunqiu 61. Gou He means his kinship with Hui does not need to be made closer by hastening to him. https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/book/NGJ89241199901548688299/chapter/1lwkpf90xscoe

proposals.before: He said, "If Heaven lets the demon bandit prevail and he gets to carry out his treason, the principle of uncle and nephew needs no guest-retainer to grow closer.
proposals.after: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.
proposals.reason: A Jinshu witness reads 奔馳 for the packet’s 賓士, confirmed independently by the parallel in Shiliuguo chunqiu 61. Gou He means his kinship with Hui does not need to be made closer by hastening to him. https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/book/NGJ89241199901548688299/chapter/1lwkpf90xscoe

units.zh: 如其罪極逆銷，天盈其罰者，守忠執志，臣之體也。
units.en: If Heaven punishes the traitor, a subject stands by his oath.
units.literal: If his crime reaches its limit and treason melts, Heaven filling his punishment, keeping loyalty and holding resolve—that is the body of a subject.

proposals.before: If Heaven punishes the traitor, a subject stands by his oath.
proposals.after: If instead his crimes reach their limit, his rebellion comes to nothing and Heaven visits its full punishment on him, my duty as a subject is to remain loyal and hold to my resolve.
proposals.reason: Restore the extinction of the rebellion when its guilt has reached its height and the minister’s determination to remain loyal.

units.zh: 違親叛君，臣之所恥。」
units.en: Betraying sovereign for kin would shame me."
units.literal: To violate kin and betray the lord is what a subject shames.

proposals.before: Betraying sovereign for kin would shame me."
proposals.after: To turn against my kin or betray my ruler would shame me.”
proposals.reason: The two coordinated phrases are turning against one’s kin and betraying one’s ruler.

units.zh: 泓善其忠恕，加金章紫綬。
units.en: Yao Hong honored him with gold seal and purple ribbon.
units.literal: Hong praised his loyal forgiveness and added gold seal and purple ribbon.

proposals.before: Yao Hong honored him with gold seal and purple ribbon.
proposals.after: Hong commended his loyalty and consideration and awarded him a gold seal with a purple ribbon.
proposals.reason: 忠恕 gives Hong’s express commendation of Gou He’s loyalty and consideration.

units.zh: 姚紹率輕騎先赴難，使姚洽、司馬國璠將步卒三萬赴長安。
units.en: Yao Shao raced ahead while Yao Qia and Guofan brought thirty thousand foot toward the capital.
units.literal: Yao Shao led light horse first to the crisis, sent Yao Qia and Simo Guofan leading thirty thousand foot to hurry to Chang'an.

proposals.before: Yao Shao raced ahead while Yao Qia and Guofan brought thirty thousand foot toward the capital.
proposals.after: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Restore Shao’s light cavalry and distinguish the full compound surname Sima in Sima Guofan; see s0131.

proposals.before: Yao Shao led light horse first to the crisis, sent Yao Qia and Simo Guofan leading thirty thousand foot to hurry to Chang'an.
proposals.after: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Restore Shao’s light cavalry and distinguish the full compound surname Sima in Sima Guofan; see s0131.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 恢從曲牢進屯杜成，紹與恢相持於靈台。
units.en: Yao Hui camped at Ducheng; Yao Shao met him at Lingtai.
units.literal: Hui advanced from Qulao and camped at Ducheng; Shao and Hui faced each other at Lingtai.

proposals.before: Yao Hui camped at Ducheng; Yao Shao met him at Lingtai.
proposals.after: Yao Hui advanced from Qulao and camped at Ducheng. He and Yao Shao faced one another at Lingtai.
proposals.reason: Restore Qulao as point of departure and the standoff rather than merely a meeting.

units.zh: 姚贊聞恢漸逼，留甯朔尹雅為弘農太守，守潼關，率諸軍還長安。
units.en: Yao Zan rushed back from Tong Pass, leaving Yin Ya to hold the river.
units.literal: When Zan heard Hui pressed gradually, he left Ningyin Yin Ya as Hongnong grand administrator guarding Tong Pass, led all armies back to Chang'an.

proposals.before: Yao Zan rushed back from Tong Pass, leaving Yin Ya to hold the river.
proposals.after: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Yin Ya holds the Ningshuo title, is made governor of Hongnong and guards Tong Pass. Zan leads his armies back on hearing that Hui is drawing near.

proposals.before: When Zan heard Hui pressed gradually, he left Ningyin Yin Ya as Hongnong grand administrator guarding Tong Pass, led all armies back to Chang'an.
proposals.after: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Yin Ya holds the Ningshuo title, is made governor of Hongnong and guards Tong Pass. Zan leads his armies back on hearing that Hui is drawing near.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 泓謝贊曰：「元子不能崇明德義，導率群下，致禍起蕭牆，變自同氣，既上負祖宗，亦無顏見諸父。
units.en: Yao Hong told Yao Zan: "I have failed the ancestors and shamed my uncles with these kin revolts.
units.literal: Hong thanked Zan, saying, "Yuanzi cannot brighten virtue and righteousness or lead the host below, causing disaster to rise from the inner wall and change to come from same-blood kin—already above I fail the ancestors, below I have no face to see the uncles.

proposals.before: Yao Hong told Yao Zan: "I have failed the ancestors and shamed my uncles with these kin revolts.
proposals.after: Hong acknowledged his fault to Zan: “I, Yuanzi, have failed to uphold and make known the way of virtue and righteousness or to lead my subordinates. I have let disaster arise within my walls and rebellion break out among my own brothers. I have failed my ancestors and am ashamed to face my uncles.
proposals.reason: 謝 is an acknowledgment of fault here. Yuanzi blames his failure to lead by virtue for the troubles within his own house and rebellion among his brothers.

proposals.before: Hong thanked Zan, saying, "Yuanzi cannot brighten virtue and righteousness or lead the host below, causing disaster to rise from the inner wall and change to come from same-blood kin—already above I fail the ancestors, below I have no face to see the uncles.
proposals.after: Hong acknowledged his fault to Zan: “I, Yuanzi, have failed to uphold and make known the way of virtue and righteousness or to lead my subordinates. I have let disaster arise within my walls and rebellion break out among my own brothers. I have failed my ancestors and am ashamed to face my uncles.
proposals.reason: 謝 is an acknowledgment of fault here. Yuanzi blames his failure to lead by virtue for the troubles within his own house and rebellion among his brothers.

units.zh: 懿始構逆滅亡，恢復擁眾內叛，將若之何？」
units.en: Yi first plotted rebellion and was crushed; Hui again leads hosts in inner revolt—what is to be done?"
units.literal: Yi first plotted rebellion and perished; Hui again embraces hosts in inner rebellion—what is to be done?"

units.zh: 贊曰：「懿等所以敢稱兵內侮者，諒由臣等輕弱，無防遏之方故也。」
units.en: Yao Zan said, "The reason Yi and others dared raise arms in inner insult is surely because we ministers seemed weak and had no means to check them."
units.literal: Zan said, "The reason Yi and others dared raise arms in inner insult is surely because we ministers are weak and light, without means to prevent and block."

proposals.before: Yao Zan said, "The reason Yi and others dared raise arms in inner insult is surely because we ministers seemed weak and had no means to check them."
proposals.after: Yao Zan replied, “Yi and the others dared take up arms and attack us from within surely because we, your ministers, are weak and had no means of forestalling or checking them.”
proposals.reason: Zan admits the ministers’ weakness, rather than saying they only seemed weak.

units.zh: 因攘袂大泣曰：「臣與大將軍不滅此賊，終不持面復見陛下！」
units.en: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject and the grand general will not destroy these bandits—I shall never again show my face before Your Majesty!"
units.literal: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject with the grand general will not destroy these bandits—never again shall I hold face to see Your Majesty!"

proposals.before: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject and the grand general will not destroy these bandits—I shall never again show my face before Your Majesty!"
proposals.after: Pushing up his sleeves and weeping aloud, Zan said, “Unless the grand general and I destroy this rebel, I will never again show my face before Your Majesty!”
proposals.reason: 不滅此賊 is the condition of Zan’s vow, not a prediction that he and the grand general will fail. 攘袂 is pushing up the sleeves.

proposals.before: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject with the grand general will not destroy these bandits—never again shall I hold face to see Your Majesty!"
proposals.after: Pushing up his sleeves and weeping aloud, Zan said, “Unless the grand general and I destroy this rebel, I will never again show my face before Your Majesty!”
proposals.reason: 不滅此賊 is the condition of Zan’s vow, not a prediction that he and the grand general will fail. 攘袂 is pushing up the sleeves.

units.zh: 泓於是班賜軍士而遣之。
units.en: Yao Hong paid the troops and sent them out.
units.literal: Hong thereupon distributed gifts to the army soldiers and sent them off.

proposals.before: Yao Hong paid the troops and sent them out.
proposals.after: Yao Hong distributed gifts to the soldiers and sent them off.
proposals.reason: 班賜 means distributing gifts or rewards, not paying wages.

units.zh: 恢眾見諸軍悉集，咸懼而思善，其將齊黃等棄恢而降。
units.en: Yao Hui's men wavered; Qi Huang and others defected.
units.literal: Hui's host seeing all armies assembled all feared and thought of good; his generals Qi Huang and others abandoned Hui and surrendered.

proposals.before: Yao Hui's men wavered; Qi Huang and others defected.
proposals.after: When Hui’s men saw that the armies had all assembled, fear seized them and they began to think of returning to allegiance. His general Qi Huang and others abandoned him and surrendered.
proposals.reason: Restore the sight of the assembled armies, universal fear and reconsideration, and that Qi Huang and others were Hui’s generals.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 恢進軍逼紹，贊自後要擊，大破之，殺恢及其三弟。
units.en: Yao Zan fell on Yao Hui from the rear, killed him and three brothers.
units.literal: Hui advanced the army pressing Shao; Zan struck him from the rear, greatly defeated him, killed Hui and his three younger brothers.

proposals.before: Yao Zan fell on Yao Hui from the rear, killed him and three brothers.
proposals.after: As Hui advanced against Shao, Zan intercepted him from the rear and routed him, killing Hui and his three younger brothers.
proposals.reason: Restore Hui’s advance on Shao, Zan’s decisive rout and the three brothers as younger brothers.

units.zh: 泓哭之悲慟，葬以公禮。
units.en: Yao Hong buried him with princely honors and mourned bitterly.
units.literal: Hong wept for him with extreme grief and buried him with ducal rites.

proposals.before: Yao Hong buried him with princely honors and mourned bitterly.
proposals.after: Yao Hong wept bitterly for Hui and buried him with the rites of a duke.
proposals.reason: 公 specifies the ducal rank of the funeral rites.

units.zh: 至是，王鎮惡至宜陽。
units.en: Wang Zhen'e had reached Yiyang.
units.literal: By this time Wang Zhen'e had reached Yiyang.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 毛德祖攻弘農太守尹雅于蠡城，眾潰，德祖使騎追獲之，既而殺晉守者奔固潼關。
units.en: Mao Dezu attacked Hongnong Grand Administrator Yin Ya at Li city; the host broke and Dezu's cavalry seized him; afterward Yin Ya killed the Jin guards and fled to hold Tong Pass.
units.literal: Mao Dezu attacked Hongnong Grand Administrator Yin Ya at Li city; the host broke; Dezu sent cavalry pursuing and seized him; afterward he killed the Jin guards and fled to firm Tong Pass.

sourceDate.text: 王師漸逼

units.zh: 檀道濟、沈林子攻拔襄邑堡，建威薛帛奔河東。
units.en: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi took Xiangyi; Xue Bo ran to Hedong.
units.literal: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi attacked and took Xiangyi stockade; Jianwei Xue Bo fled to Hedong.

proposals.before: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi took Xiangyi; Xue Bo ran to Hedong.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi stormed Xiangyi stockade. Xue Bo, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Hedong.
proposals.reason: Xiangyi is a stockade; Jianwei is Xue Bo’s generalship.

proposals.before: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi attacked and took Xiangyi stockade; Jianwei Xue Bo fled to Hedong.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi stormed Xiangyi stockade. Xue Bo, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Hedong.
proposals.reason: Xiangyi is a stockade; Jianwei is Xue Bo’s generalship.

units.zh: 泓進紹太宰、大將軍、大都督、都督中外諸軍事、假黃鋮，改封魯公，侍中、司隸、宗正、節錄並如故，朝之大政皆往決焉。
units.en: Yao Hong made Yao Shao supreme commander with the yellow axe and Lu dukedom, leaving all war policy to him.
units.literal: Hong advanced Shao to grand tutor, grand general, grand commander-in-chief, commander of all military affairs within and without, granted yellow battle-axe, changed enfeoffment to duke of Lu—palace attendant, director of Sizhou, director of clan affairs, holding seal and tallies as before; great court policy all went to decide there.

proposals.before: Yao Hong made Yao Shao supreme commander with the yellow axe and Lu dukedom, leaving all war policy to him.
proposals.after: Hong promoted Shao to grand minister, grand general, grand commander-in-chief and commander of all military affairs at court and in the provinces. He granted him the yellow axe and changed his fief to the dukedom of Lu. Shao retained his offices as palace attendant, metropolitan inspector and director of the imperial clan, his staff of authority and his oversight of the Secretariat. All major matters of court policy went to him for decision.
proposals.reason: 太宰 is grand minister, distinct from grand tutor. Restore every new appointment and the retained attendants’, inspector’s and clan offices, staff of authority and oversight of the Secretariat. 大政 encompasses major court policy beyond war.

units.en: He sent Yao Shao with fifty thousand men to Tong Pass.

units.en: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao hit Tan Daoji from two sides.
units.literal: Yao Lü and Bingzhou Inspector Yin Zhao formed inner-outer posture and jointly attacked Daoji.

proposals.after: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao, inspector of Bingzhou, coordinated their forces inside and outside the defenses and attacked Tan Daoji from both sides.

units.zh: 道濟深壁不戰，沈林子說道濟曰：「今蒲阪城堅池浚，非可卒克，攻之傷眾，守之引日，不如棄之，先事潼關。
units.en: Shen Linzi urged Tan Daoji, saying, "Puban is walled and moated too strong for a quick assault; attacking bleeds the army, holding it wastes days. Abandon it and strike Tong Pass first.
units.literal: Daoji kept deep walls and did not fight; Shen Linzi persuaded Daoji, saying, "Now Puban city is firm and moat deep—not to be taken in haste; attacking it wounds the host, guarding it draws out days—better to abandon it and first strike Tong Pass.

proposals.before: Shen Linzi urged Tan Daoji, saying, "Puban is walled and moated too strong for a quick assault; attacking bleeds the army, holding it wastes days. Abandon it and strike Tong Pass first.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji stayed behind his fortifications and declined battle. Shen Linzi urged him, “Puban’s walls are strong and its moat is deep. We cannot take it quickly. An assault would cost us men, and waiting here would waste days. Better abandon it and turn first to Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: Restore Daoji’s refusal of battle behind his defenses before Linzi offers advice.

units.zh: 潼關天限，形勝之地，鎮惡孤軍，勢危力寡，若使姚紹據之，則難圖矣。
units.en: Tong Pass is Heaven's barrier, a place of advantageous terrain; Zhen'e is an isolated army, his situation perilous and his force small—if Yao Shao is allowed to hold it, he will be hard to deal with.

units.en: Yao Zan took seven thousand palace guards to Pu ford.

units.en: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo; towns collapsed toward the capital.
units.literal: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi leading more than ten thousand to enter Shangluo; place after place mostly abandoned cities and towns and fled to Chang'an.

proposals.after: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo with more than ten thousand men. In many places people abandoned their cities and garrisons and fled to Chang’an.
proposals.reason: Restore the ten-thousand-plus force, and make clear that people abandoned towns and fled to Chang’an.
